1994 Williams FW16 Driven by Ayrton Senna in His Final Season Is Up for Grabs for the First Time
14 photos
Photo: RM Sotheby's
I'm not entirely sure why that is so, but the past few weeks have seen an unprecedented number of vehicles somehow tied to Formula 1 legend Ayrton Senna come to light. First, the Honda NSX the Brazilian used while in Europe, then a couple of 1991 McLaren MP4/6A racers, and now a Williams FW16.
Of these four cars, the Williams is perhaps the one with the best story. Not only because it was born the same year the legendary driver passed, but because it was driven by the man in his final months on planet Earth, and it then entered the possession of his family, who kept it for three decades.
The race car I'm talking about is one of two surviving Williams FW16s driven by Senna, chassis FW16B-01. The car was not driven by the man in actual races, only during warm-up and testing, but that probably doesn't decrease its value in the slightest.
Senna climbed on board the racer at Interlagos and Jerez, with the car covering a total distance of 523 miles (842 km) between the two tracks . Following Senna's fatal crash in San Marino, the F1 car was updated and continued to serve the needs of the Williams crew.
It's what happened after the season ended that brings a lot of value to the car. You see, when Senna joined the team at the end of 1993, the team made him a promise that, should Williams win the 1994 Constructors’ World Championship, the driver would be gifted a chassis.
The team won the championship that year, but Senna was no longer around to receive the car. So Williams did the next best thing and gifted the car to the Brazilian's family. They held on to it for exactly 30 years.
Chassis FW16B-01 was sold for the first time to an undisclosed person back in 2024, during a private sale. As such, we don't know how much the buyer paid for it, but we do know that now, for the first time through a public auction, the current owner hopes to get as much as $6 million for it.
The car, unrestored and all original, is going under the RM Sotheby’s hammer later this month in New York, betting not only on its connection to the three-time Formula 1 champion, but also on the fact that, throughout 1994, it was also driven by other greats of this sport, including Nigel Mansell, Damon Hill, and David Coulthard.
As a fine touch, the car is selling with a little extra: the personal seat of the Brazilian driver. It remains to be seen if the right crowd is in the house when the hammer falls – naturally, we'll keep an eye on things and report back once we know more.
